identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Shree Jagannatha Temple at Puri is the seat of Jagannatha worshipped with Balabhadra, Subhadra and Sudarshana. The temple administration describes Jagannatha as representing, directly or indirectly, all the gods and goddesses known to the Hindu world, an integrative character that is distinctive to this shrine. The temple is the source of the Ratha Jatra, in which the deities leave the sanctum each year and are drawn in chariots to the Gundicha Temple.

governance.establishedEra: Ancient origins; current structure 12th century CE · Built under Somavamshi and Ganga kings

narrative.summaryIntro:
Jagannath Temple in Puri, Odisha, is one of the four cardinal pilgrimage sites (Char Dham) and ranks among the most important temples in Hinduism. The temple is dedicated to Jagannath (a form of Krishna) along with his siblings Balabhadra (Balarama) and Subhadra. The main spire stands at a height of approximately 65.76 meters and dominates the Puri skyline.

The temple is renowned for its annual Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival), one of the most spectacular religious processions in the world, where millions of devotees gather to witness the deities being pulled through the streets in massive wooden chariots. The temple's rich traditions and architectural magnificence make it a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major spiritual center.
narrative.documentedHistory:
The present temple was built in the twelfth century CE and stands on a raised stone platform of about ten acres. At roughly 214 feet the temple administration describes it as one of the tallest monuments in the subcontinent.

The complex is enclosed by two concentric compound walls, the outer Meghanada Prachira and the inner Kurma Prachira, within which stand some thirty subsidiary shrines in addition to the main temple. The temple maintains a very large kitchen that cooks the deities' food offerings and the Mahaprasad distributed to devotees.

visitingInfo.dressCode: Traditional attire; strict dress code for temple entry
visitingInfo.entryRules: The temple administration states that only Hindus are allowed inside the temple. Visitors who are not Hindus cannot enter the enclosure; the administration notes that parts of the temple can be seen from the Emar Matha building near the eastern gate, which is the usual external viewing point. Darshan is also suspended for fifteen days each year after the Snana Yatra held on the full moon day of Jyestha, when the deities are held to be unwell and are kept out of public view (the Anasara period).
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Ritual times shift with the temple's own observances and darshan is closed outright for the fifteen days after Snana Yatra and altered through Ratha Jatra. Confirm current darshan arrangements with the Shree Jagannath Temple Administration on +91-6752-222002 or through shreejagannatha.in before travelling. The administration warns that it never accepts donations or offerings from devotees for online puja and that other sites claiming to take such payments are not authorised.

shrines.deityOrSubject: Jagannatha, Balabhadra, Subhadra, Chakra Sudarshana, Bhudevi, Sridevi and Madhaba

The eastern and principal gate of the temple; the chariots are stationed near it during Ratha Jatra.

The first lamp offering of the day.
Removal of the previous night's dress and floral decoration.
Worship of the sun, followed by Dwarapala Puja, worship of the gate guardians.
The morning food offering, the principal dhupa of the day.
The offering made in the Bhoga Mandapa, from which Mahaprasad is sold to the public.
The midday food offering. The official schedule lists it without a stated clock time.

festivals.gregorianRuleOrDate: Ashadha Shukla Dwitiya, the second day of the bright fortnight of Ashadha; falls in June or July
festivals.duration: About twelve days, ending with the deities' return to the temple
festivals.significance: The defining festival of the temple, in which the deities leave the sanctum and are drawn in chariots to the Gundicha Temple, where they stay nine days.
festivals.processionOrRituals: The deities are brought out in the Pahandi procession to the chariots stationed near the Singhadwar, in the order Sudarshan, Balabhadra, Subhadra and Jagannatha. Hera Panchami falls on the fifth day, when Lakshmi visits the Gundicha Ghar; Hari Sayan Ekadasi on the tenth day; and the Adharapana Bhoga offering on the twelfth. The festival is also known as Gundicha Jatra and Ghosha Jatra.
festivals.crowdNote: Draws very large crowds to Puri; access and traffic in the town are heavily controlled through the festival.

festivals.festivalNameEn: Snana Yatra and the Anasara period
festivals.gregorianRuleOrDate: Snana Yatra falls on the full moon day of Jyestha; falls in May or June
festivals.duration: Followed by fifteen days during which darshan is not possible
festivals.significance: After the ceremonial bathing of the deities on the Jyestha full moon, the deities are held to fall ill and are withdrawn from public view for fifteen days. This is the one long annual closure of darshan and it materially affects visit planning.

mantras.title: Jagannathashtakam (verse 1)
mantras.textOriginal:
कदाचित्कालिन्दीतटविपिनसङ्गीतकरवो
मुदा गोपीनारीवदनकमलास्वादमधुपः ।
रमाशम्भुब्रह्मामरपतिगणेशार्चितपदो
जगन्नाथः स्वामी नयनपथगामी भवतु मे ॥
mantras.transliteration:
kadācitkālindītaṭavipinasaṅgītakaravo
mudā gopīnārīvadanakamalāsvādamadhupaḥ |
ramāśambhubrahmāmarapatigaṇeśārcitapado
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapathagāmī bhavatu me ||
mantras.meaning: May Lord Jagannātha become visible to my eyes — he who at times makes music in the groves on the Yamunā's bank, who like a bee joyfully tastes the lotus faces of the cowherd women, and whose feet are worshipped by Lakṣmī, Śiva, Brahmā, Indra and Gaṇeśa.
mantras.editorNotes: Pre-populated 2026-09-28 from a published text; hidden until the temple priest confirms it is recited here. Source notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. Source prints variant readings inline: "var कवरो" (for करवो, line 1) and "var भीरी" (line 2) — removed from the text. DISAGREEMENT: vignanam line 2 reads "mudābhīrī nārīvadana…" (मुदाभीरीनारी-, "the Ābhīra (cowherd) women") where the source reads "मुदा गोपीनारी-" — this is exactly the source's own "var भीरी" variant. Same meaning; the source reading was kept. Rest matches.
